text:
emma.h: Hi all, first-day panic check. I kicked off the Buildkite pipeline for `redwood/search-svc` and it fails right away during the artifact publish with a 403 from GitHub. I'm brand new so not sure what I missed.

deploy-bot: Build #2 failed - step: publish-artifacts (exit code: 1)
```
Uploading artifacts to https://uploads.github.com/repos/redwood/search-svc/releases/9/assets
POST https://uploads.github.com/repos/redwood/search-svc/releases/9/assets -> 403 Forbidden
Error: POST https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/search-svc/releases/9/assets: 403 Forbidden
```

raj: Welcome Emma! Most common cause here is the pipeline doesn't have a RELEASE_TOKEN (masked) with repo scope. We don't rely on GITHUB_TOKEN in Buildkite pipelines for release uploads. Did onboarding give you a release token?

emma.h: I didn't get any token. The onboarding checklist mentioned CI access but I assumed the pipeline would already have secrets.

ci-oncall-bot: Note: New hires should not create personal long-lived tokens. Request a bot token via #eng-infra or use the release-operator service account. See pinned message.

ops-kate: @emma.h I can add a temporary scoped bot token to the pipeline so you can get unblocked. Quick question: Are you running the publish step in a branch PR or a main-branch pipeline? Some org settings restrict app-scoped tokens for forks.

emma.h: It's a branch PR from my fork. Could that be it?

raj: Yes - if it's a forked PR, GitHub may mask secrets. For forks we usually trigger a dedicated e2e job from the org pipeline or use a release dry-run. For now, add a temp SECRET_RELEASE_TOKEN to the pipeline and re-run the specific publish step from the Buildkite UI (Rebuild -> Rebuild from here).

ops-kate: Temporary token added as SECRET_RELEASE_TOKEN (masked). Note: I'll scope it minimal (repo:public_repo or repo as needed) and rotate it after you replace with release-operator.

emma.h: Re-ran the failed step and the upload now returns 201 Created. Thanks so much ":tada:"

michael: Follow-ups: 1) eng-infra to document the fork vs org pipeline behavior in the new-hire checklist. 2) Add a preflight in our pipelines to print a clear error if SECRET_RELEASE_TOKEN missing instead of cryptic 403. 3) Consider upgrading to the release-operator flow so tokens aren't person-bound.

raj: I'll open a tiny PR against the onboarding docs and file a ticket for the preflight. Glad your first build didn't scorch your morning.

ci-oncall-bot: Build #2 (re-run) passed - step: publish-artifacts :white_check_mark:
